edges.description: Tick inoculation introduces B. miyamotoi into human tissues and blood, where the spirochete surface can block complement attack.
Complement evasion lets spirochetes resist innate bacteriolysis long enough to establish bloodstream infection.
The bacteremic relapsing-fever Borrelia population carries variable major-protein systems that can switch expressed surface antigens.
Bacteremia manifests as acute high fever.
The systemic febrile syndrome commonly includes chills.
The systemic febrile syndrome commonly includes headache.
The systemic febrile syndrome commonly includes joint pain.
Acute infection commonly lowers the platelet count.
Acute infection commonly lowers the leukocyte count.
Acute infection commonly raises circulating hepatic transaminases.
Rare disseminated infections reach the central nervous system, especially in immunocompromised patients.
Bacteremic waves drive relapsing febrile episodes.
CNS infection manifests with meningeal or encephalitic disease.

evidence.snippet: We describe a case-patient in Minnesota, USA, who had meningeal symptoms of 1 month duration. B. miyamotoi infection was diagnosed by Gram staining on cerebrospinal fluid and confirmed by sequencing.

nodes.description: B. miyamotoi persists as a bloodstream relapsing-fever Borrelia infection whose bacteremic burden drives fever, systemic symptoms, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and elevated hepatic transaminases.

nodes.description: B. miyamotoi resists human complement-mediated killing; the outer-surface protein CbiA binds Factor H and complement components, preserving Factor H cofactor activity and inhibiting complement deposition and terminal-complex assembly on the spirochete surface.

evidence.reference_title: The relapsing fever spirochete Borrelia miyamotoi resists complement-mediated killing by human serum.
evidence.snippet: Growth inhibition assays revealed that B. miyamotoi is strongly resistant to complement-mediated bacteriolysis.

evidence.reference_title: Immune evasion of Borrelia miyamotoi: CbiA, a novel outer surface protein exhibiting complement binding and inactivating properties.
evidence.snippet: Functional analyses revealed that CbiA interacted with complement regulator Factor H (FH), C3, C3b, C4b, C5, and C9.

nodes.description: Antibiotic therapy clears B. miyamotoi spirochetemia and prevents further relapse; doxycycline is used for uncomplicated acute disease, and ceftriaxone has clinical and in vitro support for severe or CNS disease.

evidence.reference_title: Humans infected with relapsing fever spirochete Borrelia miyamotoi, Russia.
evidence.snippet: A single course of ceftriaxone or doxycycline appeared to clear B. miyamotoi infection.

evidence.reference_title: In Vitro Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Clinical Isolates of Borrelia miyamotoi.
evidence.snippet: Clinical isolates of B. miyamotoi are highly susceptible to doxycycline, azithromycin, and ceftriaxone in vitro.
